## Target, authority and independence

Review target is M1 implementation at b8f87a4c against source baseline ffb58ecb: four canonical pilot files, coupled profile/placement validator and tests, archive profile test, generated current v0.5.1 candidate metadata/index, and M1 implementation/walkthrough evidence. The larger branch range includes upstream proposal/design/delivery artifacts; those are governing basis, not claimed M1 implementation changes. Current work is m1 ready and m2 pending; the activity assigns independent Code Review. User-authorized continuation is handled through explicit current v2 operations, not a retired stored automation adapter or inferred legacy receipt route.

Current approved upstream packages are design-review-r2 and delivery-review-r2. Skill remains sha256:6c15e11c170ba7886439ba6db6c6cfd220438532b154d19be65fc0e424cfa767; System remains sha256:7b1b603cc7fb2f79ab5dabd1f275e58884a19f612a663a45bfab3a4ed03fd8f5; approved plan remains sha256:5f1f00d9e756e084670fb0acf094f7f45a25a850fbc1de88f9ea4fd0cd9260c4. Original Design/Delivery reviews inspected pre-implementation pilot/validator subjects as baseline evidence. This M1 realizes their expressly allocated changes; those original subjects are not current pilot conformance claims and were not retargeted. Governing requirements, plan allocation and ownership decisions remain unchanged and applicable. Current implementation proof binds the new exact subjects separately.

The parent implementation actor authored this slice. Reviewer /root/independent_design_review authored none of its implementation, tests, metadata or walkthrough. Earlier independent Design assessment was review activity, not engineering authorship. The same nonauthor now independently inspected the actual M1 changes, required procedures, tests and current proof. No implementation, activity or work state was edited by this reviewer.

## Actual-diff and substantive assessment

The common proposal path now exposes purpose, role, input/target selection and invocation classification before the short recording boundary. Review similarly establishes independent task and mode selection before recording construction. The complete original scoped v2 construction profile moved into each existing required reference, including context selection, subject reads, contract/revision identity, targeted operations, conflict/recovery, preservation and no-approval boundaries. Proposal's reference now points to its own scoped procedure and qualifies the stable pointer by project governance. The ordinary paths need no recording method; governed/durable and late-trigger paths still require the full method before dependent action. No new shared dependency was introduced.

Proposal-review's scope-failure cleanup retains every actionable condition and the unadopted project's changes-requested rule while explicitly deferring adopted combined conditions to the existing assessment resource. The material-status paragraph is likewise scoped to unadopted projects. Existing specialist gates, full artifact assets, trigger predicates and shared policy resources retain their bytes. This is a useful navigation/coherence improvement: the reader can select ordinary work without traversing storage construction, and required references no longer delegate their read procedure to removed parent text. It is not an improvement inferred solely from a token count or passing validator.

The validator selects the two exact reference paths independently of the removed Explicit recording heading, requires mapping/body boundary/classification trigger, rejects unreadable/escaped/missing references and validates required profile content in the selected reference. Its non-pilot inline branch remains intact. Proposal-review placement takes the current v2 branch when the new boundary is present; old document-grammar fixture coverage remains separate and no retired store support is added. Whole skill validation also checks the required pilot boundary, so removing the marker cannot silently pass the full package. Archive comparisons now observe the full selected reference on each supported adapter.

## First-pass checklist

| Item | Result | Evidence and rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Spec alignment | pass | Four selected files implement SKL-SR-16-19's inspected outcomes and SKL-SR-02-15/20 preservation under M1/TG-01-03. Scope, specialist policies, names, assets and proof limits remain as approved. |
| 2. Test coverage | pass | New production-validator cases cover both pilots without the old heading, missing boundary/trigger, malformed revision content, absent reference despite unrelated/inline complete text, escaped symlink, unreadable UTF-8, unknown mapped path and wrong v2 placement. Existing non-pilot retired-writer protection remains. Focused tests fail before and pass after; full 357-test skill suite passes. |
| 3. Edge cases | pass | Tests directly observe package/profile failures; the source/artifact walkthrough separately covers ordinary/governed/advisory/formal paths, late durable triggers, malformed governed signals, untriggered missing resources, stale authority and interrupted writes. No claim confuses optional runtime loading with complete package validity. |
| 4. Error handling | pass | Exceptions produce explicit errors for absent/unreadable/escaped selected resources; missing required profile/trigger fails. Loaded methods keep conflict reread, explicit recovery and unsafe-authority stops; missing content cannot be reconstructed. |
| 5. Architecture boundaries | pass | Existing body/reference/assets decomposition and original path ownership remain. Project pointer policy is consumed without new fields or schema. Workflow, assessment and CLI retain decision/persistence boundaries. |
| 6. Compatibility | pass | Direct comparison confirms exactly four changed canonical files and 133 unchanged files, including all 17 non-pilot bodies and pilot assets/shared resources. Added asset-fixture resources satisfy the current package precondition without removing asset assertions. Existing historical placement grammar remains covered. |
| 7. Security/privacy | pass | No secrets, external publication, customer installation, new execution permissions or policy adoption are introduced. Path containment protects the selected reference; late triggers and recording do not grant mutation or continuation authority. |
| 8. Derived artifact currency | pass for M1 candidate scope | Observed full generation/adapter passes and Gate A/B. Independently compared all three available temporary candidate archives to current metadata hashes/sizes, current metadata hash to releases.json and historical index entries to baseline. Archive profile test compares selected reference bytes on Codex, Claude Code and opencode. No live installed/customer currency claim. |
| 9. Unrelated changes | pass | Canonical byte comparison and diff show only the four approved skill files plus their coupled tests/validator and explicitly allocated current metadata dependency. Upstream authored governance artifacts are separate prior work; M1 does not retire source definitions. |
| 10. Validation evidence | pass | Named logs and current registered m1-implementation check bind the exact changed subjects and report focused red/green, 357 skill tests, seven generation tests, 158 adapter tests and Gate A/B. Negative release-fixture diagnostics appear inside a passing adapter suite, not actual failed release execution. Evidence is adequate for M1's package and bounded semantic claims. |

## Test-maintenance and proof assessment

No test was deleted. The old scope assertions combined current and unconditional historical judgment wording; replacement assertions retain all four scope-defect conditions and both explicit adopted/unadopted branches. Existing asset fixtures now carry the complete selected recording package instead of bypassing its preconditions. Profile-preservation assertions and archive comparisons follow the actual new normative location; missing reference tests deliberately show that unrelated text cannot rescue it. These changes maintain useful detection rather than preserving incidental location/prose.

The independent source/artifact assessment accepts the walkthrough's seven-section proposal and summary review result for their stated fixture assumptions. The reviewer assessed actual instructions, policy selection, conditional groups and complete reference reachability; this does not assert execution of an external agent or universal output accuracy. CLI retry/persistence semantics are unchanged and consumed by the moved procedure, so no new CLI engine test is required for text relocation. Existing package tests and narrow mutations supply direct mechanical proof at the changed boundary.

## Checks actually performed and evidence reused

Reviewer performed git diff/status inspection, complete reads of the four changed pilot files and M1 evidence, relevant full plan/source and test/validator inspections using cat/sed/rg, exact primary context/review reads, subject inspect --content full --max-bytes 8388608, Python raw-byte comparison of all 137 baseline canonical files, three candidate archive hash/size comparisons, and current metadata/index plus historical-entry comparisons. All byte/hash comparisons passed. Initial broad context exposed a 20-of-22 partial result; required reviews were expanded with full review show and final scoped context uses an explicit sufficient limit before recording. No absence was inferred from omitted context.

Inspected implementation executions: python scripts/test-skill-validator.py -k targeted (three red, then three passing tests), python scripts/test-skill-validator.py (final 357 pass), python scripts/validate-skills.py (19 skills), python scripts/build-skills.py and --check, python scripts/test-build-skills.py (seven pass), python scripts/test-adapter-distribution.py (158 pass, 624.881 seconds), and python scripts/validate-adapters.py --version v0.5.1 --adapter-root for the generated candidate (Gate B pass). Current m1-implementation subjects match exact inspection; no later engineering changes were present. These existing executions were not redundantly rerun by the reviewer. Prose/whitespace checks are author evidence with their stated limits.

No material finding or unresolved necessary decision was identified. Remaining risk and work are explicitly M2 source transfer, archive navigation and consumer reconciliation, then fresh final whole-change Code Review and distinct Verify. This milestone review supplies none of those conclusions. Route may now record M1 completion and proceed to its authorized M2 allocation.
